---

## Fill-Realism Correction

**Problem identified:** Original sim filled at `sig.entry_price +/- 0.25 friction`.
Live `entry_manager` places MARKET orders; by 1m bar close the price has already
moved through the breakout level.  Worst case: 2026-07-01T14:00 SESSION_BREAKOUT
BUY booked +$102.34 — the detection bar closed ABOVE the TP, meaning live never
opens the position.

**Correction method:**

    detection bar  = 1m bar whose open time == entry_time in the CSV
    new_entry_px   = bar_close + 0.25  (BUY)
                   = bar_close - 0.25  (SELL)
    friction       = 0.25 (spread/2 = 0.15 + slippage = 0.10)

    Phantom guards (dropped trades -- live never books P&L on them):
      Beyond-TP (all trades):
        BUY:  new_entry_px >= tp  -> drop (market already through TP)
        SELL: new_entry_px <= tp  -> drop
      Beyond-SL (non-trailing trades only):
        BUY:  new_entry_px <= sl  -> drop (market already through the stop;
        SELL: new_entry_px >= sl     live is stopped out instantly)

    Trailing rows carry the RATCHETED stop in the CSV `sl` column, so the
    signal stop is not recoverable at CSV level; the engine's own guard
    (run_sim) applies the beyond-SL guard to trailing strategies too, using
    sig.stop_loss at detection time.

Exit prices are kept unchanged.  **This is NOT valid for TRAIL exits**: the
trail seeds its high-water mark from the entry fill, so every subsequent
ratchet -- and therefore the exit bar and exit price -- is fill-path-dependent.
The CSV correction consequently CANNOT produce a corrected number for S96
(the only trailing strategy); see the S96 caveat below.

### Phantom example -- 2026-07-01T14:00 SESSION_BREAKOUT

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| strategy | SESSION_BREAKOUT |
| entry_time | 2026-07-01T14:00:00+00:00 |
| side | BUY |
| Old entry_px (sim) | 4047.560 (sig.entry_price + 0.25) |
| Detection bar close | 4099.245 |
| Corrected entry_px | 4099.495 (bar_close + 0.25) |
| TP | 4098.980 |
| Phantom | True (4099.495 >= 4098.980) |
| Old pnl_usd | +102.34 |
| Corrected pnl_usd | DROPPED |

A beyond-SL example: 2026-04-22T05:17 KRONOS_S97_SNAP_SCALPER SELL — corrected
entry 4762.040 is already above the signal stop 4760.820, so live is stopped
out on fill; dropped (old pnl -$8.22).

| Correction delta (raw->corr) | -445.94 | ex-S96: +49.68 |

**S96 caveat — corrected S96 numbers are artifacts in BOTH directions:**
S96's `sig.entry_price` is the last closed H1 bar's close — up to ~1 hour
stale.  During crash days (e.g. 2026-06-17: five consecutive BUYs at an
identical stale 4379.8 while the market traded ~4264–4272) the CSV correction
refills at market but keeps exits anchored to stops derived from the phantom
entry, converting phantom losers into phantom winners.  The raw ungated S96
figure (-$4,946) books losses on entries live would never fill at those
prices, and the "corrected" S96 figure manufactures winners from those same
phantom trades — so neither number is quotable.  S96's real number requires
an engine re-run with market fills + both phantom guards; the CSV correction
cannot produce one.  Use the ex-S96 view below for the reliable gating-edge
signal.

## Ex-S96 View

S96 (KRONOS_S96_H1_MOMENTUM) supplied +$212.87 gated / -$4,946 ungated in the
raw sim and dominates the apparent gating edge, but its corrected numbers are
not computable from the CSVs (TRAIL limitation above).  TRENDING regime was
only 5.7% of the 3-month window, giving 10 gated and 144 ungated S96 trades.
The ex-S96 view isolates the measurable edge from the three other strategies
(S95, S97, SESSION_BREAKOUT).

| Mode | Raw Net $ (0.02L) | Phantoms | Corrected Net $ (0.02L) | Corrected Net $ (0.01L) |
|------|------------------:|---------:|------------------------:|------------------------:|
| Gated ex-S96 | +364.49 | 4 | +42.13 | +21.07 |
| Ungated ex-S96 | -148.78 | 10 | -99.10 | -49.55 |
| **Delta ex-S96 (G-U)** | **+513.27** | -- | **+141.23** | -- |

**This ex-S96 corrected pair — gated +$42.13 vs ungated -$99.10 — is THE
rubric-relevant comparison.**  The gating edge survives correction: corrected
gated positive, corrected ungated negative.

Two caveats on reading the pair.  First, the gated and ungated runs do not
share identical candidate entries: the regime gate can delay when a strategy
first detects a setup (gate-delayed detection), so the pair compares two
different entry sets rather than the same trades filtered.  Second, a +$141
ex-S96 delta over 3 months at 0.02 lots is directional evidence that the gate
helps — it is not proof of positive expectancy.

Raw ex-S96 delta = +513.27; corrected ex-S96 delta = +141.23 (27.5% of the raw
ex-S96 delta survives correction).  The large compression reflects
SESSION_BREAKOUT's sensitivity to late fills.

## Live Sizing Note

deploy_manager.py sets MANAGER_CHILD_LOT=0.01 (half the sim's 0.02 lots).
All live P&L figures are exactly half the 0.02L sim figures.

| Scenario | Net 3 months (0.02L sim) | Net 3 months (0.01L live) |
|----------|-------------------------:|--------------------------:|
| Corrected gated combined | +131.42 † | +65.71 † |
| Corrected ex-S96 gated | +42.13 | +21.07 |
| Corrected gated S96 only | +89.29 † (uncertain sign, ±~$100) | +44.64 † |
| Corrected gated SESSION_BREAKOUT | +84.69 | +42.35 |

† S96 term has uncertain sign, ±~$100 (TRAIL limitation); rows containing it
are unreliable — the ex-S96 row is the dependable planning figure.

Kill-switch: $150 floor is calibrated to 0.02L sim behaviour.  At 0.01L live,
a $150 intraday loss equals a ~3-sigma adverse run -- effectively 2x tighter
than the sim's equivalent risk budget.  Consider raising the kill-switch to $200
or lowering individual child lots once paper mode confirms fill quality.

## REVISED VERDICT

**RECOMMEND arming PAPER mode (arm_mode=PAPER).**

**The rubric-relevant comparison is the ex-S96 corrected pair: gated +$42.13
vs ungated -$99.10 at 0.02L over 3 months (delta +$141.23).**  The corrected
gated combined is +$131.42 at 0.02L (+$65.71 at 0.01L), but that figure
includes an S96 term of uncertain sign bounded ~±$100 (TRAIL limitation), so
the ex-S96 pair carries the evidential weight.  The gated/ungated entry sets
differ due to gate-delayed detection, so the pair compares entry sets, not
the same trades filtered.  A +$141 ex-S96 delta over 3 months at 0.02L is
directional evidence that the gate helps, not expectancy proof.  Measurable
edge is concentrated in SESSION_BREAKOUT (+$84.69 corrected gated, 53
trades); S95 is near breakeven; S97 is negative in both modes.

Live promotion is contingent on all of the following:

1. **Sensitivity grid** -- re-run with --sensitivity flag to confirm the gating
   edge is not parameter-sensitive.  A parameter-sensitive delta sign-flip would
   downgrade to DO NOT RECOMMEND.

2. **S96 real number from an engine re-run** -- get S96's real number from an
   engine re-run with market fills + both phantom guards — the CSV correction
   cannot produce one.  TRENDING was only 5.7% of this window, producing 10
   gated S96 trades; confirm the TRENDING gate is airtight, and do not scale
   S96 until that re-run and a minimum 30-trade live sample are available.

3. **Paper fills confirming corrected expectancy** -- paper target for the
   measurable (ex-S96) book is ~+$42 at 0.02L / ~+$21 at 0.01L over 3 months.
   If paper shows consistent underperformance, investigate SESSION_BREAKOUT
   entry timing further.

4. **S97 review (consider NOT arming)** -- KRONOS_S97_SNAP_SCALPER is negative
   in both raw (-$62.82) and corrected (-$43.32) gated modes.  Current
   recommendation is PAPER only; exclude S97 from any live arming until it shows
   positive corrected expectancy on a fresh window.

5. **S95 status** -- KRONOS_S95_SESSION_BREAKOUT is near breakeven (+$0.64 raw,
   +$0.76 corrected gated).  Acceptable as a regime-filtered scalper at small
   size; does not drive expectancy.
